beats.narration: Checkpoint one had two parts: assemble the settings for a trusted payments refactor, and place a human gate. The requirements: auto-approve edits, never run destructive shell commands, and the production env file must never be readable. Haven't done it? Pause here first.

Part one: the correct assembly is pieces C and D. C allows the safe npm run commands, and denies R M and git push. That's the deterministic shell gate. D denies reads of the production env file, which holds at the settings layer no matter what the session asks for. Why not the others? Piece A sets default mode, which prompts on nearly every edit. The scenario demanded auto-approved edits. Piece B is bypass: it removes the exact oversight the scenario requires, plus the protected-path guard. And piece E allows every shell command outright. The opposite of a gate. Notice one nuance: a classifier mode could also catch destructive commands, but the scenario asked for predictable, deterministic gating. That's what explicit deny rules give you: no judgment call involved.

elements.code:
C: allow ["Bash(npm run:*)"]
   deny  ["Bash(rm:*)", "Bash(git push:*)"]
D: deny  ["Read(.env.production)"]

elements.text:
deterministic shell gate + path denial
that holds all session
✗ B bypass — removes oversight AND the path guard
✗ E allow-everything — the opposite of a gate
explicit deny > classifier when you need predictability

beats.narration: Part two: mid-refactor, the agent proposes a change to a deployment configuration file that several production services read. Where's the gate? Answer B: a human reviews and approves before the write executes. The settings auto-approve edits, sure. But the session default doesn't answer the per-action question. A wrong value in that file is hard to undo, and its blast radius reaches far beyond the file. Option A treats the default as the answer. Option C removes every prompt. And option D, reviewing at the next pull request, reviews a change that already reached production. After is too late.

elements.text: deploy config file, read by prod services — gate where?
✓ B — human approves BEFORE the write executes

hard to undo + blast radius beyond the file
= the worst-case question says: gate it
✗ D — PR review happens AFTER production felt it

beats.narration: The two-part pattern: deny rules make the floor deterministic, and the worst-case question places the one gate the defaults can't. Next section: durable project context.
